content.intro: This lesson covers Importing and Exporting Tabular Data as part of Data Sorting, Filtering, and Management. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Importing and Exporting Tabular Data supports repeatable analysis by organizing, cleaning, summarizing, or relating data. Preserve the raw source and reconcile a summary back to its input records. Compatibility: Check Microsoft’s function reference for the target Excel version, platform, and update channel. Dynamic-array spill behavior and some newer functions are not available in every legacy installation.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Importing and Exporting Tabular Data focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: CSV and TXT files; Delimiters and character encoding; Import-time data types; Preserving identifiers and leading zeros. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.expected_output: Calculates a date/time result using serial values; the exact interpretation depends on cell values, formatting, locale and whether holidays or overnight intervals matter.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Enter real Excel date/time values, not ambiguous text. Apply an appropriate number format and test boundaries such as month-end, blanks and overnight durations.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: Start with a small, known dataset for importing and exporting tabular data. Apply the example above, compute or inspect at least one result independently, then deliberately try a blank, duplicate, boundary, or not-found case where relevant.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates importing and exporting tabular data. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

content.task: Build or inspect an Excel example that demonstrates importing and exporting tabular data; use the example to verify one normal and one edge case, and write down any version or tool dependency.
task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: Calculates a date/time result using serial values; the exact interpretation depends on cell values, formatting, locale and whether holidays or overnight intervals matter.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
